title: Elevated-Temperature Tribo-Corrosion Response of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: A cast eutectic high-entropy alloy (likely Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni system) with a lamellar dual-phase (B2 + bcc) microstructure
recollection.intervention: High-temperature tribo-corrosion testing using a pin-on-disk tribometer under a NaCl solution spray at 400–600 °C
recollection.structure: Eutectic lamellae of ordered B2 phase embedded in a disordered bcc matrix, with a thermally grown oxide scale (mixed spinel/Cr2O3) at the sliding interface
recollection.mechanism: Synergistic oxidative wear: at elevated temperatures the alloy forms a protective oxide film which is continuously disrupted by sliding, leading to dynamic repassivation and smearing of oxide tribo-films
recollection.results: At 500 °C the coefficient of friction stabilized around 0.55, the wear rate was ~1.8 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/Nm, and the corrosion current density under wear was reduced by ~30% compared to room-temperature testing

score.note: The recollection misstates the apparatus, environment, and temperature range: the study used immersed reciprocating ball-on-flat testing at 25–100 °C, not pin-on-disk testing under NaCl spray at 400–600 °C. It also incorrectly identifies the lamellar phases as B2+bcc rather than L12+B2. The general idea of sliding-induced oxide/passive-film disruption and repassivation is relevant, but it misses the key temperature-dependent transition from abrasion at 25 °C to minimum-wear polishing at 50 °C and unstable oxidative/third-body wear at 100 °C. All recalled numerical results are inconsistent with the paper.
